title: Grammar and Syntax of Nadi-9: Descriptive Field Notes
author: Dr. S. K. Narang, Field Linguistics Unit

rules.statement: Nadi-9 primarily follows Canonical SOV (Subject - Object - Verb) word order in declarative sentences. Adverbs and temporal expressions precede the direct object.
examples: Pani zolo drav-ina (The water slowly flows)

rules.statement: Present continuous and imperfective aspect is marked by the verbal suffix -ina attached to the verb root.
Simple past tense is marked by suffix -va.
Simple future tense is marked by suffix -is.
Standard verbal negation is formed with prefix na- bound to the verb stem (e.g. na-mani, na-chhod). It never occurs as a detached post-verbal particle in formal speech.

Kinship address incorporates prefixes depending on seniority. Elder brother in intimate familial address uses prefix da- (da-bhai). Respected mother takes honorific modifier tari (tari ama). Senior patriarchal figures take prefix vad-.
unsettled_questions: Does da-bhai apply when siblings are estranged or formally disputing inheritance?

rules.statement: Urban speakers frequently borrow standard trade terms, but traditional narrative dialogue rejects English or high-court Persianisms unless indicating bureaucratic satire.
examples: Hari vasan bheetar lyo (pure native terms preferred over loanwords)

rules.statement: Yes/no questions conclude with sentence-final particle ki. Content questions place question words (kit, kyo) immediately preceding the verb.
